configKeys.range: no spec range; defineList with a per-entry validator: 3 to 5 semicolon-separated parts, parts[0] and parts[1] must parse as ResourceLocations, duration_in_ticks >= 0, amplifier >= 0 (optional, default 0), chance between 0.0 and 1.0 (optional, default 1.0). The "new entry" template offered by the config UI is minecraft:apple;minecraft:speed;200;0;1.0.
configKeys.effect: Item-to-potion-effect table applied when a living entity finishes eating the item. Format: item_id;effect_id;duration_in_ticks;amplifier;chance. Several lines may target the same item (all of them are applied, each rolled separately). Entries whose item or effect is not registered are dropped silently at cache load. Every listed item is additionally made always-edible via the FOOD data component.

configKeys.defaultValue: ["minecraft:beetroot_soup;6;", "minecraft:mushroom_stew;2;", "minecraft:rabbit_stew;2;", "minecraft:melon_slice;2;"] - note the trailing semicolons, which split drops, so chance defaults to 1.0
configKeys.range: no spec range; defineList with a per-entry validator: 2 or 3 semicolon-separated parts, parts[0] must parse as a ResourceLocation, thirst_amount >= 0, chance between 0.0 and 1.0 (optional, default 1.0). Template: minecraft:beetroot_soup;6;1.0.
configKeys.effect: Item-to-thirst table. Format: item_id;thirst_amount;chance. Only ever read when Tough As Nails is loaded (loadThirstEffects returns immediately otherwise, FoodEffectsModule.java:121-124) and only applied to Players; the restored value is capped at 20. One entry per item (a HashMap, so a second line for the same item overwrites the first). The items ARE made always-edible even without Tough As Nails.

shortDescription: Allows adding potion effects to food items via configuration.
notes:
EVIDENCE BASE: src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/modules/food_effects/{FoodEffectsModule.java (311 lines), config/FoodEffectsConfig.java (136), compat/TANIntegration.java (20), client/ThirstTooltipData.java (9), client/ThirstClientTooltip.java (59)}; .../standalone/food_effects/FoodEffectsStandalone.java (@Mod("vpa_food_effects") -> StandaloneModuleBootstrap.boot); VanillaPlusAdditions.java:20 (import), :166 (registerModule), :472-490 (ClientModEvents, @EventBusSubscriber(bus=MOD, value=Dist.CLIENT)); build.gradle:150 (TAN), :432 (standaloneModules entry), :614-616 (coreJar includes), :641-642 (moduleJar includes), :507-530 (renderModuleToml); src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml:89-95 (toughasnails, type="optional", versionRange="[10.1.0,)", ordering="NONE", side="BOTH"); README.md:144-148 + :238. No shouldInitialize() and no isEnabledByDefault() override anywhere in the module (grep), so Module.java:73 (default true) applies. No DeferredRegister, no KeyMapping, no RegisterCommandsEvent, no mixins (the build.gradle:432 descriptor carries neither 'mixins' nor 'clientMixins', and vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json has no food entry). No docs/modules/food_effects.md yet.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES - three independent mechanisms that are easy to conflate:
1) LivingEntityUseItemEvent.Finish (:152-213), server side only (:159 early-returns on level().isClientSide()). For every cached EffectEntry of that item it rolls entity.getRandom().nextFloat() <= chance and calls entity.addEffect(...). The handler takes the generic LivingEntity, so ANY living entity that finishes eating a configured item gets the effects, not only players.
2) Thirst restoration (thirst_effects list), Player only and Tough As Nails only (:203-212), via TANIntegration.applyThirst -> ThirstHelper.getThirst(player).setThirst(min(current + amount, 20)) (TANIntegration.java:16-19).
3) ModifyDefaultComponentsEvent (mod bus, :258-272): the FOOD data component of every item named in EITHER list is rebuilt with alwaysEdible().

BUG 1 - saturation is double-converted, and for the default config it is converted TWICE OVER (FoodEffectsModule.java:290-292). The code reads existingFood.saturation() - already the absolute value - and feeds it back into FoodProperties.Builder.saturationModifier(); build() then re-applies FoodConstants.saturationByModifier(nutrition, modifier) = nutrition * modifier * 2 (verified in the project's own decompiled 1.21.1 sources under build/tmp/.cache/expanded/zip_8a9cb.../: FoodProperties.java:113-115, FoodConstants.java:30-32). Worse: NeoForge's ModifyDefaultComponentsEvent.modify() applies each patch IMMEDIATELY (ModifyDefaultComponentsEvent.java:55-62 -> Item.modifyDefaultComponentsFrom, Item.java:112-117, which reassigns Item.components), and new ItemStack(item) reads exactly that map (ItemStack.java:260-261). processItemForFoodComponent therefore compounds for every item listed more than once. With the SHIPPED defaults: mushroom_stew (vanilla 6 / 7.2) is on both lists -> 6*7.2*2 = 86.4 after the first pass, 6*86.4*2 = 1036.8 after the second; rabbit_stew (10 / 12) -> 240 -> 4800; beetroot_soup (6 / 7.2) -> 86.4 -> 1036.8; enchanted_golden_apple, create:bar_of_chocolate and create:chocolate_glazed_berries are each listed twice in food_effects and compound the same way; single-listed items get one pass (cookie 0.4 -> 1.6, melon_slice 1.2 -> 4.8). In game the practical effect is bounded, because FoodData.add() clamps saturationLevel to the current foodLevel (FoodData.java:20-23) - so every configured food simply saturates to the maximum instead of its vanilla value.

BUG 2 - the FOOD rebuild drops two of the six FoodProperties fields. The record is (nutrition, saturation, canAlwaysEat, eatSeconds, usingConvertsTo, effects) (FoodProperties.java:17-19); the builder call chain only sets nutrition, saturation(-modifier), alwaysEdible and the copied effects, so usingConvertsTo and eatSeconds fall back to the defaults (empty / 1.6 s). With the DEFAULT config this hits mushroom_stew, rabbit_stew and beetroot_soup, which vanilla builds via Foods.stew(...) = ...usingConvertsTo(Items.BOWL) (Foods.java:87) and which Player.java:2192-2200 uses to hand the empty bowl back. So with this module enabled on defaults, eating a stew returns no bowl. Likewise any configured fast food (eatSeconds 0.8, e.g. dried kelp) would be reset to the 1.6 s default.

TIMING LIMIT: ModifyDefaultComponentsEvent fires once during mod loading. The effect/thirst CACHES reload on config load (FoodEffectsConfig.onConfigLoad:57-61 -> reloadEffectCache) and on load-complete (AbstractModule:139 -> onLoadComplete -> reloadEffectCache), but the always-edible / FOOD-component change needs a game restart to follow a config edit. Also: items from the thirst_effects list are made always-edible even when TAN is absent (processItemForFoodComponent runs over both lists unconditionally, :263-271), and a non-food item on either list is turned into a 0-nutrition, 0-saturation, always-edible item (:297-303).

DEDICATED-SERVER HAZARD, with an in-repo precedent: onGatherTooltipComponents (:245-256) subscribes the CLIENT-only event class net.neoforged.neoforge.client.event.RenderTooltipEvent.GatherComponents on the COMMON NeoForge.EVENT_BUS (registered at :58 via NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this)), with no Dist guard and no @OnlyIn, inside the same class that carries the server logic. Every other module in this repo keeps client event handlers in a separate modules/<id>/client/ class - and end_oxygen once had exactly this pattern (@SubscribeEvent public void onRenderGuiLayer(RenderGuiLayerEvent.Pre) in EndOxygenModule) until commit 3a43685 (2026-05-11) "Fix dedicated-server client class loading in End Oxygen", CHANGELOG: "Client-only GUI/Render-Code in eine dedizierte Client-Event-Klasse ausgelagert, damit auf Dedicated-Servern keine Client-Klassen mehr aus Common-Code geladen werden". food_effects was last touched functionally on 2026-05-08, three days before that fix, and never got the same treatment. The repo does not contain a stack trace or a test proving what happens on a dedicated server, so do NOT assert either "crashes" or "harmless" in the docs - but this is a known-bad pattern here, not an open question of style. (For the record, food_effects is the only user of RenderTooltipEvent and of ItemTooltipEvent in the repo.)

STANDALONE-JAR GAP (provable from the build script, not tested in game): the ClientTooltipComponent factory for ThirstTooltipData is registered ONLY in VanillaPlusAdditions.ClientModEvents (VanillaPlusAdditions.java:488-489). coreJar includes core/**, util/**, standalone/core/**, assets and logo.png (build.gradle:613-619) and moduleJar_food_effects includes modules/food_effects/** + standalone/food_effects/** (build.gradle:640-643) - neither contains VanillaPlusAdditions.class. So in the standalone vpa_food_effects.jar + TAN case, hovering a thirst-configured item adds a TooltipComponent with no registered factory and ClientTooltipComponent.create() throws IllegalArgumentException("Unknown TooltipComponent") (decompiled ClientTooltipComponent.java:19-29). The bundle jar is unaffected. Additionally the generated per-module toml (renderModuleToml, build.gradle:507-530) declares only vpa_core/neoforge/minecraft as required plus 'incompatible' against the bundle - it does NOT carry the optional toughasnails dependency the bundle's mods.toml has (ordering is NONE there anyway, so this is metadata only).

TAN ICON COUPLING (verified against the shipped jar libs/ToughAsNails-neoforge-1.21.1-10.1.0.13.jar): ThirstClientTooltip blits toughasnails:textures/gui/icons.png at hardcoded UVs (0,41) full droplet and (8,41) half droplet, assuming a 256x256 sheet. The jar's icons.png is indeed 256x256 and carries a full water droplet at (0,41) and the matching half droplet at (8,41), so the coordinates are correct for 10.1.0.13 - but any TAN update that moves those icons breaks the tooltip silently. All TAN ids used in the defaults exist in that version too (effects climate_clemency, thirst, internal_warmth, internal_chill; items cactus_juice, chorus_fruit_juice, glow_berry_juice, melon_juice, sweet_berry_juice; lang keys desc.toughasnails.heating_consumed / cooling_consumed).

DEBUG LOGGING IS NOISY AND PUBLIC: with debug_logging on, EVERY finished use-item (any eating/drinking, not just configured food) broadcasts "[DEBUG] Consumed food item: ..." plus "Food cache entries: N" plus one chat line PER CACHED ITEM - and MessageBroadcaster.broadcast sends to the whole server player list, not just the level (MessageBroadcaster.java:29-51, used at FoodEffectsModule.java:166-186). The cache is keyed by Item, so N is the number of distinct RESOLVABLE items, not the number of config lines: the 21 default food_effects entries cover 18 distinct items (enchanted_golden_apple, create:bar_of_chocolate and create:chocolate_glazed_berries appear twice each), so with Create + TAN + Rotten Creatures installed that is about 20 chat lines per bite for every player online; in pure vanilla only cookie and glow_berries resolve, so it is 4. Worth a warning in the docs.

NAMING TRAP FOR THE DOC WRITER: "thirst" means two opposite things here. The thirst_effects list RESTORES thirst; the default food_effects entries "minecraft:golden_apple;toughasnails:thirst;600;0;0.25" (plus enchanted golden apple and golden carrot) apply TAN's thirst MOB EFFECT (dehydration) at 25 % chance. Both are on by default.

SMALL THINGS: (a) the default thirst entries carry a trailing semicolon ("minecraft:beetroot_soup;6;"); String.split drops trailing empty strings, so parts.length is 2 and chance falls back to 1.0 - harmless, reads like a typo, and the validator accepts it. (b) The chance test is <=, so chance 0.0 can still fire on an exact 0.0 roll (:193, :205). (c) Unresolvable item ids (Items.AIR) and unknown effect ids (null) are skipped SILENTLY; the warning only appears with debug_logging on (:106-113, :142-144), while parse exceptions always log at error level (:116, :147) - and inside processItemForFoodComponent exceptions are swallowed entirely (:307-309). (d) minecraft:enchanted_golden_apple appears twice in the defaults (thirst effect + climate_clemency); that is intentional, effectCache holds a List per item - but see BUG 1 for the side effect. (e) Orphan lang string: "desc.vpa.toughasnails.thirst_restored" exists in en_us.json:85 and in de_de/de_at/fr_fr/es_es/cs_cz, but no Java code references it - the thirst tooltip renders droplet icons plus an optional " (NN%)" and nothing else. There are no other food_effects lang keys. (f) The heating/cooling tooltip lines use TAN's OWN translation keys desc.toughasnails.heating_consumed / cooling_consumed and match on hardcoded ids toughasnails:internal_warmth / internal_chill (:37-38, :232-240), i.e. they appear for any configured item carrying those effects.

Later touches: d0e807e (checkstyle), 98379b6 (2026-05-06), 3d26329 "Add Tough As Nails integration and food effects expansion" (2026-05-08, first tag v0.10.0), 3277b27 (thirst_restored translation), a11fb79 "Add graphical thirst tooltip" (2026-05-08, first tag v0.10.2), 27c7405 (2026-07-01, standalone jars, beta.23), 376995f + 68d11fd (2026-08-27, builders tea removed from the thirst defaults). So "since 0.6.0" is true for the module, but thirst support exists only since v0.10.0 and the droplet tooltip only since v0.10.2.

README CHECK: README.md:144-148 and the optional-mod row README.md:238 are accurate as far as they go ("configured items become always edible", "Tough As Nails support (optional): thirst restoration and heating/cooling tooltips", "Thirst-related food effects are skipped"). They do not mention the saturation inflation, the lost bowl on stews, or that the always-edible change only follows a config edit after a restart.
